summary: A floating action button: a prominent button for the main action of a screen, such as composing a message.
overview:
A Floating Action Button (FAB) is a circular button that represents the primary action on a screen. It supports four color roles and two variants.

An icon-only FAB needs an accessible name: set aria-label, or a tooltip, which is used when no aria-label is set. With neither (and no label), a warning is logged once.

Set toggle for a toggle FAB with aria-pressed; selected does nothing without it. Link mode (href) stays supported on the FAB.
cssprop: --fab-container-elevation-level: Elevation level of the FAB. Defaults to 3.
fires: change - Dispatched by a `toggle` FAB after a click flips `selected`.

cssProperties.description: Background color of the FAB container.
cssProperties.name: --fab-container-color:

cssProperties.description: Text and icon color of the FAB label.
cssProperties.name: --fab-label-text-color:

cssProperties.description: Corner radius of the FAB. Defaults to var(--shape-corner-large).
cssProperties.name: --fab-container-shape:

cssProperties.description: Elevation level of the FAB. Defaults to 3.
cssProperties.name: --fab-container-elevation-level:

events.description: Dispatched when the FAB is clicked. Not dispatched while `loading`, `soft-disabled` or `skeleton`.
events.name: click

events.description: Dispatched by a `toggle` FAB after a click flips `selected`.
events.name: change

attributes.name: label
attributes.description:
Optional label text for the extended FAB variant.
When set, the FAB displays both the icon and a text label.

attributes.name: loading
attributes.description:
When true, the FAB is busy: it shows a spinner in place of its icon, sets `aria-busy="true"`
and ignores clicks, like `soft-disabled`.

attributes.name: color
attributes.description:
The color role of the FAB.
`"surface"` uses the surface color role.
`"primary"` uses the primary color role.
`"secondary"` uses the secondary color role.
`"tertiary"` uses the tertiary color role.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
The style variant of the FAB.
`"tonal"` uses container colors.
`"filled"` uses solid role colors.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
The size of the FAB.
`"sm"` renders a small FAB (40×40dp).
`"md"` renders a standard FAB (56×56dp). This is the default.
`"lg"` renders a large FAB (96×96dp).

attributes.name: lowered
attributes.description: If `true`, the FAB is in a lowered (resting) state with reduced elevation.

attributes.name: tooltip
attributes.description:
Tooltip text shown on hover. Without a `label`, also the accessible name when no
`aria-label` is set.

attributes.name: skeleton
attributes.description: When true, renders the FAB as a placeholder skeleton while the page loads.

attributes.name: toggle
attributes.description:
When true, the FAB is a toggle button: it renders `aria-pressed`, flips `selected` on click
and fires `change`.

attributes.name: selected
attributes.description: The pressed state of a `toggle` FAB. Has no effect without `toggle`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: When `true`, the button is disabled and cannot be interacted with. Reflects to the `disabled` attribute. Defaults to `false`.

attributes.name: soft-disabled
attributes.description:
When `true`, the button is visually styled as disabled and cannot be interacted with, but remains focusable.
Use this in combination with `disabledReason` to communicate why the button is unavailable.
Reflects to the `soft-disabled` attribute. Defaults to `false`.

attributes.name: disabled-reason
attributes.description:
A human-readable explanation of why the button is disabled or soft-disabled.
Rendered as a visually hidden tooltip and linked via `aria-describedby` for accessibility.
Maps to the `disabled-reason` attribute.

attributes.name: throttle-delay
attributes.description: Sets the delay for throttle in milliseconds. When undefined (default), no throttle is applied.

attributes.name: href
attributes.description: The URL to link to. When set, the component renders as an `<a>` element.

attributes.name: target
attributes.description:
Where to open the linked URL: `"_self"` (default), `"_blank"`, `"_parent"`, `"_top"` or a
frame name. Pair `"_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

attributes.name: rel
attributes.description: The relationship of the linked URL to the current page, as the native `rel` attribute.

attributes.name: download
attributes.description:
Downloads the linked URL instead of navigating to it; the value is the suggested file
name. Only applies with `href`.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description:
What activating the element does in a form: `"submit"` (default) submits it, `"reset"`
resets it and `"button"` does nothing.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The value sent with the form, paired with `name`, when this element submits it.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form.

label: Field
summary: The box around a form control, with its label, required mark, helper, error or warning text and a character count.
overview:
The field draws the frame of a form control: the label with a required mark, the bordered box with field-start and field-end slots, and a footer with helper, error or warning text and a character count. Wrap a custom control in it to match the built-in fields.

The default variant fills its box with surface-container-lowest, so it stands out on cards and dialogs as well as on the page. outlined has no fill (the outline alone marks it) and filled uses surface-container-highest, as in Material 3. Disabled follows M3: the text at 38%, the outline at 12% and a 4% fill. Read-only keeps the label and value at full contrast in a faint box, so it reads as information.

The outlined variant is the M3 outlined text field: its label rests inside the empty field and, on focus or with a value, floats into a notch in the outline's top edge. The outline is drawn in parts (start, notch, end), so the notch needs no background and the field works on any surface. The outline is 1px, 2px while focused.
cssprop: --field-label-rest-top - Where the outlined label's resting line is centred, from the top of the box. Defaults to the middle; multi-line fields set it to their first line.

cssProperties.description: The box's fill. Defaults to `surface-container-lowest` (default variant), `surface-container-highest` (filled) or none (outlined).
cssProperties.name: --field-container-color

cssProperties.description: The outline's resting width. Defaults to 1px on the outlined variant.
cssProperties.name: --field-outline-width

cssProperties.description: Where the outlined label's resting line is centred, from the top of the box. Defaults to the middle; multi-line fields set it to their first line.
cssProperties.name: --field-label-rest-top

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Label text shown above the field input.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description: When true, marks the field as required and shows a required indicator.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: When true, the field and its slotted input are disabled.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: When true, the field and its slotted input are read-only.

attributes.name: skeleton
attributes.description: When true, renders the field in a loading skeleton state.

attributes.name: helper-text
attributes.description: Helper/hint text shown in the field footer.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: When true, the field is in an error state and `errorText` is shown.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Error message displayed when `error` is true.

attributes.name: warning
attributes.description: When true, the field is in a warning state and `warningText` is shown.

attributes.name: warning-text
attributes.description: Warning message displayed when `warning` is true.

attributes.name: text-count
attributes.description: Character / word count string displayed at the trailing end of the footer.

attributes.name: focused
attributes.description: When true, applies focused styling (controlled externally by the slotted input).

attributes.name: populated
attributes.description: When true, applies populated styling (controlled externally by the slotted input).

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual variant of the field container.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description:
Height of the field box: `sm` (2.5rem, the default, the same as a default button), `md`
(3.5rem) or `lg` (4rem). `data-density` on an ancestor shortens it further.

attributes.name: host
attributes.description: Reference to the host input element; used to forward click-on-label focus.

label: Fieldset
summary: Groups related fields under a headline and disables them together.
overview:
Fieldset renders a native <fieldset> with a <legend>, so assistive technology announces its fields as a group named by the headline; supporting-text describes the group. The fields stack with the standard gap between fields, which follows the density.

disabled disables every form control inside, as on a native fieldset: Peacock fields and buttons, other form-associated elements, and native inputs, selects, text areas and buttons, however deeply nested and including ones added later. Disabled controls are left out of form submission. A slotted control is not inside the shadow <fieldset> as far as the browser is concerned, so the fieldset sets disabled on each control itself, and turning it off re-enables only the controls it disabled. A nested wc-fieldset is disabled as a whole and handles its own controls.
slot: - The fields.
cssprop: --fieldset-gap - Space between the fields. Defaults to `--spacing-200`, less with density.
example:
```html
<wc-fieldset headline="Shipping address" supporting-text="Where should we send the order?">
  <wc-input label="Street" name="street"></wc-input>
  <wc-input label="City" name="city"></wc-input>
  <wc-select label="Country" name="country"></wc-select>
</wc-fieldset>
```

cssProperties.description: Space between the fields. Defaults to `--spacing-200`, less with density.
cssProperties.name: --fieldset-gap

slots.description: The fields.

attributes.name: headline
attributes.description: Title of the group, rendered as its `<legend>` and used as its accessible name.

attributes.name: supporting-text
attributes.description: Text under the headline that describes the group, linked with `aria-describedby`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables every form control inside, like a disabled native `<fieldset>`.

label: File Upload
summary: A drop zone and file picker that collects files into a list, for the app to upload.
overview:
File upload collects files: the person drops them on the zone, or activates it (click, Enter or Space) to open the system file picker. Chosen files are listed with their name and size and a button that removes them. The component uploads nothing itself: the app listens for change, uploads files however it likes and reports back per file with setFileState(file, { progress, error, done }), which shows a progress bar, an error or a done mark on that file.

accept, max-size (bytes per file) and max-files (with multiple) decide what is added. Files that do not fit are left out, listed in a short message under the zone, and reported in a reject event. Without multiple, a new file replaces the chosen one. A file that is already listed is not added twice. Adding, removing and rejecting files is announced to screen readers.

Inside a <form> the files are submitted under name, like a native file input; required blocks submission while no file is chosen, and form.reset() clears the list. readonly shows the list without the drop zone and the remove buttons.
fires: remove - Dispatched when the person removes a file, before `change`.
cssprop: --file-upload-drop-zone-min-block-size - Minimum height of the drop zone.
example:
```html
<wc-file-upload
  label="Photos"
  name="photos"
  accept="image/*"
  multiple
  max-files="5"
  max-size="5000000"
  helper-text="Up to 5 images, 5 MB each"
></wc-file-upload>
```

customElement.description: Formats a size in bytes with `Intl`, in decimal units: "512 bytes", "1.5 MB".

label: Filter Bar
summary: The faceted filter row above a table or list: search, filter chips and saved views.
overview:
Describe the filters the person can use with filters, an array of { key, label, type, options?, placeholder? }. type picks the control the filter is edited with: select, multiselect, text, date-range or boolean (a switch).

"Add filter" opens a menu of the filters not in use yet. Each active filter is a dismissible chip, "Label: value"; a click (or Enter) on it opens its control in a popover, and its dismiss button (or Delete) removes it. "Clear all" removes every filter and keeps the search text.

value holds the active filters by key: a string for select and text, an array of strings for multiselect, start/end ISO dates for date-range and a boolean for boolean. With search, the search text is under the reserved key q. The value is plain JSON, so it can go in the URL. Every committed change fires change with { value }; typing in the search box fires input, and change once the text is committed (Enter, blur or clear).

Saved views: views lists named values, shown in a views menu with "All" (which clears the value). Picking one sets view to its id ('' for "All"), applies its value and fires view-change, then change. With saveable the menu has "Save view", which fires view-save with the current value; store it and add it to views. The views menu shows when there are views or saveable is set. view stays as it is when the person edits the filters afterwards.

Accessibility: the bar is a group named by label (default "Filters"). The chips are one tab stop: the arrow keys move between them (mirrored in right-to-left), Home and End jump to the ends. Each popover is a dialog named after its filter; Escape closes it and returns focus to the chip. Removing a filter is announced through a polite live region.

Filters from a sentence. With search and a provider that offers parse (ADR-030002), typing a sentence such as "urgent hardware incidents in Pune" offers Turn into filters. The provider gets the sentence and the filter definitions (never record values) with target: 'filter-bar', and answers with a value; only known filters with valid values are kept, and words it could not map stay as search text. The new chips are marked with a sparkle and one Suggested badge whose clear button puts the previous filters back; editing or removing a chip accepts it. no-ai turns this off.
fires: view-save - Dispatched when the person picks "Save view".
example:
```html
<wc-filter-bar id="bar" search></wc-filter-bar>
<script>
  bar.filters = [
    { key: 'status', label: 'Status', type: 'select',
      options: [{ label: 'Open', value: 'open' }, { label: 'Closed', value: 'closed' }] },
    { key: 'archived', label: 'Archived', type: 'boolean' },
  ];
</script>
```

customElement.description: Key of the search text in `value`.

label: Focus Ring
summary: A ring drawn around a control while it has keyboard focus, so people can see where focus is.
overview:
Attach it to a control with for (the control's id), by setting control, or by calling attach(); otherwise it follows its parent. It shows when the control gains focus and matches :focus-visible, and hides on blur or a pointer press, so mouse and touch users do not see it. When several focus rings sit inside one component, only the first to handle a focus event reacts.

inward draws the ring inside the control's edge, for controls inside a container. visible reflects whether the ring shows and fires visibility-changed when it changes. The ring is hidden from assistive technology.
fires: visibility-changed - Dispatched whenever `visible` changes.

events.name: visibility-changed
events.description: Dispatched whenever `visible` changes.

attributes.name: visible
attributes.description: When true, the focus ring is visible. Toggled automatically based on `:focus-visible` state.

attributes.name: inward
attributes.description: When true, the ring animates inward instead of outward (for use inside containers).

label: Form
summary: Wraps a native form with an error summary, dirty tracking, a busy state and server errors.
overview:
Put a native <form> inside wc-form: <wc-form><form>…</form></wc-form>. The form stays in the page (light DOM), so every Peacock field and native control joins it as usual; a form inside wc-form's own shadow root could not see slotted fields.

Validation. On submit, wc-form checks every field. While any is invalid the form is not submitted: an error summary (a danger wc-alert) at the top lists each field's label and message as links that focus the field, and focus moves to the summary. The summary updates as fields are fixed and goes away when all are. Peacock fields also show their message under the field. With no-summary, focus moves to the first invalid field instead. A novalidate form, or a submit button with formnovalidate, skips validation as natively.

Submitting. A valid submission fires a cancelable submit CustomEvent whose detail.value is the form data as a plain object (repeated names become arrays), read through FormData. Call preventDefault() to save it yourself; otherwise the form submits natively to its action. The native submit event stops at wc-form, so listeners see one event. Set loading while saving: submit buttons become busy (wc-button gets loading, native buttons are disabled), the form gets aria-busy, and further submits are ignored.

Unsaved changes. dirty is true while any field's value differs from its value when the form was set up, and dirty-change fires when it flips. Call markClean() after a successful save to make the current values the new baseline; resetting the form also makes it clean. warn-unsaved asks the browser to confirm leaving the page while the form is dirty.

Server errors. setErrors({ email: 'Already taken' }) marks the named fields invalid with those messages (through setCustomValidity()) and lists them in the summary. An error clears when its field changes. A name that matches no field is listed in the summary without a link, for errors about the whole form.

Drafts from the assistant. suggest(values) fills named fields with suggested values, each marked Suggested with its reason (ADR-030002). While any field holds a suggestion, a banner at the top says the form was drafted by the assistant and offers Clear all (hide-draft-banner turns it off). Editing a field accepts its suggestion; submitting accepts the rest, and submit's detail.suggested lists the fields that were still suggested, so the change can be recorded as made through the assistant. With AI off, suggestions are ignored and the form is unchanged.
slot: - The native `<form>`.
fires: dirty-change - Dispatched when `dirty` flips.
cssprop: --form-summary-gap - Space between the error summary and the form.
csspart: draft-banner - The banner shown while fields hold the assistant's suggestions.

customElement.description: Turns `FormData` into a plain object; a name that appears more than once becomes an array.

label: Generative View
summary: Shows an answer of the assistant as Peacock components, from JSON checked against an allow-list, never as HTML or code.
overview:
When an answer is better as a few numbers, a chart or a table than as text, the assistant can return it as JSON nodes, such as {"type": "stat", "props": {"label": "Open incidents", "value": 42}}, and this view lays them out with Peacock components (ADR-030002). It renders only the components and props of its catalog, which is generated from the component manifest and an allow-list: layout (stack, grid, card, divider), text, numbers, charts, tables, lists, tags, alerts, Markdown, citations and buttons. generativeViewSchema() returns the catalog as a JSON Schema for the model service.

Nothing in it can navigate, load an address or run code: there is no HTML, no href or src, no callbacks. An unknown node shows as its text, an unknown or ill-typed prop is dropped, and issues lists what was dropped. A node with an action id fires action when pressed or selected, and does nothing else: the app decides what happens, and a write is still a draft the person confirms.

Give the answer in value, as nodes or as their JSON text. With streaming the text may be cut off; the view shows what has arrived so far. Citations resolve through citations, as in wc-markdown.

It is marked "By the assistant" (badge-label changes it; hide-badge drops it where its container already marks it, such as a wc-chat-message). Like every marker of the assistant, it renders nothing while AI is off for the page.
fires: action - A node with an `action` was pressed or selected.

events.name: action
events.description: A node with an `action` was pressed or selected.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The answer: a node, a list of nodes and text, or their JSON text.

attributes.name: streaming
attributes.description: The JSON is still arriving and may be cut off.

attributes.name: citation-href
attributes.description: Address of a cited source not in `citations`; `{id}` is replaced by its id.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name of the view, such as "Open incidents by priority".

attributes.name: badge-label
attributes.description: The marker's text; defaults to "By the assistant".

attributes.name: hide-badge
attributes.description: Drops the marker, where the container already marks the answer as the assistant's.

label: Grid
summary: Lays out its children in a CSS grid of equal columns, or as many columns as fit.
overview:
The grid is a CSS grid container: the element itself has display: grid, so its children are the grid items, with no wrapper between them.

The columns come from two attributes that combine rather than exclude each other:

  • columns="3" alone: three equal columns at every width.
  • min-column-width="12rem" alone: as many columns as fit, each at least that wide (auto-fill); one column when the grid is narrower than that.
  • Both: as many as fit at that minimum width, but never more than columns.

Without either, the grid has one column (the CSS default) and only spaces its rows.

gap, row-gap and column-gap take a step of the spacing token scale, as on wc-stack (gap="200" is var(--spacing-200)); row-gap and column-gap override gap on their axis. align sets align-items and justify sets justify-items.

An item spans columns or rows with plain CSS on the item: style="grid-column: span 2", or grid-column: 1 / -1 for a full-width row.
slot: - The grid items.
example:
```html
<wc-grid columns="4" min-column-width="12rem" gap="200">
  <wc-card>One</wc-card>
  <wc-card style="grid-column: span 2">Two, twice as wide</wc-card>
  <wc-card>Three</wc-card>
</wc-grid>
```

slots.description: The grid items.

attributes.name: columns
attributes.description: Number of equal columns; with `min-column-width`, the most columns the grid shows.

attributes.name: min-column-width
attributes.description:
Minimum width of a column, as a CSS length (for example `12rem`). The grid shows as many
columns as fit, capped by `columns` when that is set.

attributes.name: gap
attributes.description: Space between rows and columns, as a step of the spacing token scale.

attributes.name: row-gap
attributes.description: Space between rows, as a step of the spacing token scale. Overrides `gap`.

attributes.name: column-gap
attributes.description: Space between columns, as a step of the spacing token scale. Overrides `gap`.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Block-axis alignment of the items in their cells (`align-items`).

attributes.name: justify
attributes.description: Inline-axis alignment of the items in their cells (`justify-items`).

label: Highlight
summary: Marks the words of a search query in a piece of text.
overview:
Highlight shows its text with each word of query marked, for search results in a knowledge base, a site search or a filtered list. Words match on their own, in any order, ignoring case and accents, so "resume" marks "Résumé".

It reads its children as plain text and never parses HTML, so text from records or a search index is safe to put in it. When the server already knows where the matches are, set ranges instead of query.

Marks use the tertiary container colour, so they differ from links and from the selection.
slot: - The text. Only its text content is used; markup in it is not rendered.
csspart: mark - Each marked run of text, a `<mark>` element.
cssprop: --highlight-color - Text colour of the marks. Defaults to `--color-on-tertiary-container`.
example:
```html
<wc-highlight query="reset password">
  If you forgot your password, choose Forgot password and reset it from the link we email you.
</wc-highlight>
```

cssProperties.description: Background of the marks. Defaults to `--color-tertiary-container`.
cssProperties.name: --highlight-background

cssProperties.description: Text colour of the marks. Defaults to `--color-on-tertiary-container`.
cssProperties.name: --highlight-color

cssParts.description: Each marked run of text, a `<mark>` element.
cssParts.name: mark

slots.description: The text. Only its text content is used; markup in it is not rendered.

attributes.name: query
attributes.description: The search query whose words are marked.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: The language to fold case in. Defaults to the nearest `lang`, else the browser's.

label: Hover Card
summary: A rich preview, such as a profile card or a link preview, shown while the pointer rests on a trigger or the trigger has keyboard focus.
overview:
The first child is the trigger, usually a link; the element with slot="content" is the card. The card opens after open-delay (500 ms) of hovering or of keyboard focus on the trigger, and closes close-delay (300 ms) after the pointer and focus have left both the trigger and the card, so the pointer can cross the gap into the card. It stays open while hovered or while focus is inside it. Escape closes it, and so does a press outside.

Unlike wc-tooltip, which is short plain text that describes its target, the card can hold links and buttons; unlike wc-popover, nothing opens it on click. The card is a supplement: the trigger keeps its own action (following the link), and everything in the card must also be reachable without it, for example on the page the link goes to.

The trigger gets aria-details pointing at the content, which screen readers announce as "has details" and let the person jump to. It gets no aria-haspopup or aria-expanded, because activating it does not open the card. Once open, the card's content follows the trigger in the Tab order.

Touch screens have no hover: a tap activates the trigger and does not open the card. Use show() from your own control if touch users need the preview.
slot: content - The card's content.
cssprop: --hover-card-width - Width of the card. Defaults to `20rem`.
fires: close - Fired when the card closes: Escape, the pointer and focus leaving, or a press outside (`light-dismiss`), or `hide()` / `open = false` (`api`).
example:
```html Ana Lima
Ana Lima

Product designer, Lisbon

Follow
```

cssProperties.description: Background of the card. Defaults to `var(--color-surface-container)`.
cssProperties.name: --hover-card-background

cssProperties.description: Padding of the card. Defaults to `var(--spacing-200)`.
cssProperties.name: --hover-card-padding

cssProperties.description: Width of the card. Defaults to `20rem`.
cssProperties.name: --hover-card-width

slots.description: The trigger: the first child element.
The card's content.
slots.name: content

events.description: Fired when the card opens.
events.name: open

events.description: Fired when the card closes: Escape, the pointer and focus leaving, or a press outside (`light-dismiss`), or `hide()` / `open = false` (`api`).
events.name: close

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the card is open.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description:
Preferred placement of the card: `top`, `bottom`, `start` or `end`, optionally with `-start`
or `-end` alignment. It flips to stay in the viewport.

attributes.name: open-delay
attributes.description: Milliseconds of hover or focus on the trigger before the card opens.

attributes.name: close-delay
attributes.description: Milliseconds after the pointer and focus leave before the card closes.

label: HTML Editor
summary: A rich-text field whose value is HTML, with the same toolbar and mentions as the Markdown editor.
overview:
Use it where the value has to be HTML, such as an email body or a CMS field. It works like wc-markdown-editor: a toolbar, a selection bubble, a slash menu, a block handle, mentions and a View source button that shows the HTML in wc-code-editor. HTML can store underline and resizable table columns, which Markdown cannot, so the HTML editor offers them.

Get and set the HTML through value; an empty editor has the value ''. Only what the editor supports is kept: other tags, attributes and scripts in a value are dropped when it loads.

Mentions. Typing a character from triggers (@ by default) fires search with { trigger, query }; answer by setting suggestions. A mention is stored as <span data-type="mention" data-id="usr_142" data-label="Ana Lima">@Ana Lima</span>.

The editor is form-associated, fires input and change with { value }, and supports required, maxlength, rows and max-rows, as the Markdown editor does.

Read-only and disabled. readonly keeps the text at full contrast and leaves only View source in the toolbar, which shows the HTML read-only. disabled dims the toolbar and the text. show-readonly-badge adds a lock badge to the toolbar in either state.
cssprop: --mention-list-max-height - Maximum height of the mention suggestion list.
fires: mention - Dispatched when a suggestion is inserted as a mention.

cssProperties.description: Background behind the text.
cssProperties.name: --rich-text-editor-background

cssProperties.description: Color of links.
cssProperties.name: --prose-link-color

cssProperties.description: Background of mention chips.
cssProperties.name: --prose-mention-background

cssProperties.description: Text color of mention chips.
cssProperties.name: --prose-mention-color

cssProperties.description: Background of inline code and code blocks.
cssProperties.name: --prose-code-background

cssProperties.description: Width of the mention suggestion list.
cssProperties.name: --mention-list-width

cssProperties.description: Maximum height of the mention suggestion list.
cssProperties.name: --mention-list-max-height

events.description: Dispatched as the content changes, after `debounce` milliseconds without typing.
events.name: input

events.description: Dispatched when focus leaves the editor after an edit.
events.name: change

label: Illustration
summary: A themed spot illustration for empty, error and success moments, such as no results, a 404 page or a finished payment.
overview:
The illustration draws the art named by name. Peacock ships eighteen: empty, no-results, empty-inbox, no-notifications, no-messages, no-files, upload, not-found, server-error, error, no-access, offline, maintenance, success, welcome, empty-cart, no-team and coming-soon. Each one is a small module loaded the first time its name is shown; registerIllustration(name, art) adds art of your own.

The art is drawn with the theme's color tokens, so it follows the theme and dark mode. The --illustration-*-color custom properties recolor every illustration at once.

An illustration is decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology, because the heading beside it says the same thing. Set label when the picture carries meaning of its own; it then has role="img" with that name.

size (sm 6rem, md 10rem, lg 15rem) sets the width through --illustration-size; a width set in CSS still wins. The height follows at 4:3. Compose empty, error and success screens from an illustration, a heading, text and buttons; it replaces wc-empty-state.

label: Inline Edit
summary: Click-to-edit text for record pages: a title, a description, a field value.
overview:
Inline edit shows value as text, or placeholder in a muted style when it is empty, with a pencil button after it. Clicking the text or the pencil button (or pressing Enter or Space on the button) opens the editor: a wc-input, or with multiline a wc-textarea. The text takes the font of its surroundings, so it can sit in a heading.

Keys: Enter saves (Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter with multiline, where Enter starts a new line) and Escape cancels. Moving focus out of the editor saves, exactly like Enter, so nothing typed is lost. A save of an unchanged value just closes the editor and fires nothing. After a save or cancel from the keyboard or the buttons, focus returns to the pencil button. show-actions adds Save and Cancel buttons after the editor.

Saving fires a cancelable change with the new text in detail.value. The contract:

  • Synchronous: do nothing. The component sets value and closes the editor.
  • Rejected: call event.preventDefault(). The editor stays open with the text; set error-text to say why.
  • Asynchronous: set loading in the handler. The editor stays open, read only, with a progress indicator. When the server answers, set loading back to false: with error-text set the editor stays open and shows the error, so the person can fix the text and save again; with error-text empty the editor closes and value becomes the saved text (set value before clearing loading to show the server's version instead). Clear error-text when you start the next save and on cancel.

With required an empty (or blank) text is not saved: the editor stays open with a message. maxlength limits the text and shows a character counter. While loading, Escape and blur do nothing: a save in flight cannot be cancelled.

label names both views for assistive technology: the pencil button is "Edit label" and the editor is named label. The label is not shown. disabled and readonly show the text without the pencil button.

Inline edit is not a form field: it is not form-associated and has no name. It edits a record that the app saves at once. For a value submitted with a form, use wc-input or wc-textarea inside a wc-form.

label: Item
summary: The layout that list items and menu items are built on, with start, text and end areas.
overview:
Not used on its own: wc-list-item and wc-menu-item render it.

Content goes in named slots: start before the text; overline, the default slot, headline and supporting-text in the text column; trailing-supporting-text and end after it; and container behind the item. The start, trailing supporting text and end areas are hidden while they are empty.

When more than one text slot has content the item sets multiline, which gives it a taller minimum height. Set multiline yourself only for server-side rendering of a two-line item, to avoid a flash of unstyled content.

Not part of the public API: use `wc-list-item` or `wc-menu-item`. It stays registered because those components render it.
example: ```html Notifications Manage alerts and reminders 3 ```

label: JSON Viewer
summary: A collapsible tree of a JSON value, such as an API response or a webhook body.
overview:
Set value to any JavaScript value from script, or to JSON text with the value attribute. Text that is not valid JSON shows an error with the parser's message. (A string set from script is shown as a string, not parsed.)

Objects and arrays expand and collapse; a collapsed one shows its size, such as {3 keys} or [12 items]. expand-depth sets how many levels start expanded (default 1, the root; all expands everything). Children are rendered only once their parent is expanded, and at most 100 at a time with a row that shows the next 100, so a large payload stays fast. Strings longer than 200 characters are cut until clicked or Enter is pressed. Values are colored with the code highlighter's syntax colors.

Hovering or focusing a row shows buttons that copy its value (strings as is, anything else as indented JSON) and its JSONPath, such as $.items[2].id.

The tree follows the WAI-ARIA tree view pattern and is one tab stop: Up and Down move between rows, Right expands a row or moves to its first child, Left collapses it or moves to its parent (mirrored in right-to-left), Home and End jump to the first and last row, * expands every sibling, and typing moves to the next row whose key starts with the typed text. Tab from a row reaches its copy buttons.

label: Kanban
summary: A board of columns whose cards the person moves by drag and drop or with the keyboard.
overview:
The board is data-driven: columns ({id, title, limit?}) and cards ({id, columnId, title, ...}), where the order of cards is the order within each column. renderCard renders a card's content; without it a card shows its title. Cards are rendered into the light DOM, so page styles reach the content, and each sits in a wrapper with role="listitem" inside its column's role="list", named by the column title.

Moving a card fires the cancelable card-move event with {cardId, fromColumn, toColumn, fromIndex, toIndex}. Unless it is canceled, the board applies the move itself and replaces cards with a new array. To confirm a move with a server first, cancel the event and apply it later with applyKanbanMove().

With a pointer, drag a card (on touch, hold it briefly first, so a swipe still scrolls). A placeholder shows where it will land, and the board and columns scroll when the card nears their edges. Escape cancels.

Cards are one tab stop. The arrow keys move focus between cards (Left and Right between columns, mirrored in right-to-left), Home and End to the first and last card of the column. Space or Enter picks the focused card up; the arrow keys then move it, Space or Enter drops it and Escape or Tab cancels. Each step is announced in a live region.

A column with a limit shows its count against it and is flagged when it holds more cards. addable adds an "Add card" button to every column, which fires card-add.
fires: card-add - Dispatched when the person presses a column's "Add card" button.

customElement.description:
Moves a card in a `cards` array the way the board does, returning a new array. Use it to apply
a `card-move` you canceled, for example once the server has accepted it.

label: Kbd
summary: Shows a keyboard shortcut as key caps, with the platform's key names and symbols.
overview:
keys takes a shortcut such as mod+shift+p and shows one <kbd> per key. mod is Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. On Apple platforms modifiers show as symbols without separators (⌘⇧P), as macOS menus do; elsewhere they show as names joined by + (Ctrl+Shift+P). platform forces one style, for documentation.

Key names: mod, ctrl, meta (cmd), alt (option), shift, enter, escape (esc), tab, backspace, delete, space, up, down, left, right, pageup, pagedown, home, end, capslock; any other key shows as written, a single letter upper-cased.

Screen readers read symbols badly, so the caps are hidden from them and a spelled-out copy is read instead, such as "Control+Shift+P". The names come from Peacock's strings and can be translated.

Without keys, the content shows as one key cap: <wc-kbd>Esc</wc-kbd>.
slot: - A key to show as written, when `keys` is not set.
csspart: separator - The `+` between keys off Apple platforms.
cssprop: --kbd-border-color - Border color of a key cap.

label: Markdown
summary: Shows Markdown as formatted text, the read view of the Markdown editor and comments.
overview:
Give the Markdown as value. It reads GitHub-flavoured Markdown (tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks) and mentions written as [@Ana Lima](mention:usr_142), the form wc-markdown-editor and wc-comment-composer store, so a saved description looks the same as it did in the editor.

It is safe for text people typed: raw HTML is shown as text, and only http(s), mailto:, tel: and relative links are followed; other links show their text only. Links open in a new tab, apart from links to # anchors.

Mentions show as chips. With mention-href they are links: {id} in it is replaced by the mention's id, for example mention-href="/users/{id}".

inline shows the Markdown as a run of text without block spacing, for a one-line summary or an activity entry.

Streaming. For an answer that arrives in pieces, set streaming and keep replacing value with the text so far. Only the last blocks are parsed again, an unfinished **, ` or link at the end is shown as it will be once complete, and a caret marks the end. The content is aria-busy until streaming is turned off, so screen readers wait for the finished text.

Citations. Links written as [2](cite:rule_88) show as wc-citation chips. citations supplies each source's headline, supporting text and address by id; citation-href (with {id}) is the address of sources it doesn't list. A chip fires select.

label: Markdown Editor
summary: A rich-text field whose value is Markdown: people format text as they type, and can view the Markdown source.
overview:
Use it where a form needs more than a textarea, such as a description, notes or a release note. People edit formatted text directly; the value is Markdown, so it stores as plain text and shows the same way in wc-markdown.

  • Toolbar. Text style, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, link, lists, checklist, quote, code block, table, divider and mention. While the caret is in a table, a Table menu adds and removes rows and columns. hide-toolbar hides it.
  • Selection bubble. Selecting text shows the inline formats and link.
  • Slash menu. Typing / inserts a block; Markdown shortcuts such as ## , - and **bold** work too.
  • Block handle. Hovering a block shows a handle to drag it and a + to insert one below.
  • View source. The last toolbar button shows the Markdown, editable, in wc-code-editor.

Mentions. Typing a character from triggers (@ by default) fires search with { trigger, query }; answer by setting suggestions, and suggestions-loading while you look. A chosen mention is stored as [@Ana Lima](mention:usr_142) and fires mention. Set triggers="" to turn mentions off.

The editor is form-associated. It fires input with { value } as the content changes (after debounce milliseconds without typing) and change when focus leaves after an edit. required blocks an empty submit, and maxlength limits the number of characters and shows a count.

rows sets the height of the empty editor in lines; it grows with the text, up to max-rows if set, and then scrolls.

Read-only and disabled. readonly keeps the text at full contrast and leaves only View source in the toolbar, which shows the Markdown read-only. disabled dims the toolbar and the text. show-readonly-badge adds a lock badge to the toolbar in either state.

label: Mention Input
summary: A multiline text field where typing a trigger character, such as the at sign, suggests people or tags to mention.
overview:
Mention input is a textarea in which a trigger character, @ by default, opens a list of suggestions at the caret. Picking one inserts the trigger and the suggestion's label as text, such as @Ana Lima, followed by a space.

value is the plain text the person sees, and it is what the field submits with a form. mentions lists the mentions in it, each {id, label, trigger, start, end}; the field keeps the positions up to date as the text changes. Editing inside a mention turns it back into plain text; Backspace right after a mention (or Delete right before it) removes the whole mention. To load saved text, set value and then mentions; entries that do not match the text are dropped.

The app supplies the suggestions: on search (detail: {trigger, query}) it sets suggestions to the matches, each {id, label, description?, avatar?}, and sets loading while it fetches them. The list shows while there are suggestions or loading is set. triggers takes several characters, such as "@#" for people and tags.

Focus stays in the textarea: Arrow Up and Down move the highlighted suggestion (aria-activedescendant), Enter or Tab inserts it, Escape closes the list. A trigger counts at the start of the text or after a space or an opening bracket or quote, so email addresses do not open the list.

It validates like wc-textarea (required, minlength, maxlength) and grows with the text with auto-grow. It is a plain-text field; for rich comments use wc-comment-composer.

label: Menu
summary: A list of actions or choices that opens next to a button or another element.
overview:
A menu opens next to an anchor element, in the browser's top layer, so it shows above dialogs, sticky headers and any parent with overflow: hidden. Items are wc-menu-item elements; a wc-divider separates groups and a wc-sub-menu nests a menu.

Keyboard: when the menu opens, focus moves to the selected item or the first enabled one. Arrow Up/Down move with wrap-around, Home/End jump to the ends, typing a letter jumps to the next item starting with it, Enter/Space activate, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger, Tab closes.

Choices: items with type="checkbox" toggle selected and keep the menu open; items with type="radio" select themselves, clear the other radio items between the same wc-dividers and close the menu. The new state is set before menu-item-activate fires.

label: Menu Item

overview:
A menu item is a button, or a link when it has an href. A selected item shows a check mark at the end; an item with a submenu shows a chevron. Put an icon in the start slot; the menu lines up the labels of items without one.

Set type="checkbox" or type="radio" to make selected accessible: the item becomes a menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio with aria-checked. A plain item only shows the check mark. Activating a checkbox item toggles it and keeps the menu open; activating a radio item selects it, clears the other radio items of its group (the items between the same dividers) and closes the menu.

A link item that stands for the current page sets current (aria-current="page").

label: Modal
summary: A dialog for content in a layer above the page, with optional header, body and footer.
overview:
The modal opens a native <dialog> with showModal(), so it renders in the browser's top layer: above sticky headers, app bars, cards and any stacking context on the page, whatever their z-index. Menus, selects and tooltips opened inside the modal render above it.

While it is open the rest of the page is inert and does not scroll; focus moves to the first element with autofocus inside it, and returns where it was when the modal closes. Escape and a click on the scrim close it (no-light-dismiss keeps it open on scrim clicks).
cssprop: --modal-max-height - Maximum height of the dialog.
fires: close - Fired when the modal closes: Escape, a scrim click, the close button, or `hide()`.
example:
```html
<wc-button onclick="document.getElementById('confirm').show()">Delete project</wc-button>
<wc-modal id="confirm" heading="Delete project?">
  This deletes the project and its 12 files. You can't undo this.
  <wc-button slot="footer" variant="text" onclick="this.closest('wc-modal').hide()">Cancel</wc-button>
  <wc-button slot="footer" color="danger" autofocus>Delete</wc-button>
</wc-modal>
```

label: Notification Center
summary: An in-app inbox behind a bell button: an unread count and a panel listing notifications by day.
overview:
The notification center is a bell wc-icon-button with a wc-badge showing the unread count. Pressing it opens a panel anchored to the bell (a full-height side sheet on phone-width screens) with the notifications, newest first, grouped under Today, Yesterday and dates, each with a relative time ("5 min. ago") formatted with Intl in the resolved locale. The panel has All and Unread filters and Mark all as read.

The app owns the data. The component never changes notifications; it fires events and the app updates the list (optimistically if it likes) and assigns a new array:

  • item-click (detail.notification, cancelable) when a notification is activated. A notification with href is a link and navigates unless the event is cancelled. Marking it read is up to the app.
  • read-change (detail.ids, detail.read) from the per-item Mark as read / unread buttons and Mark all as read.
  • dismiss (detail.notification) from an item's dismiss button.
  • load-more from the Load more button, shown while has-more is set. Set loading while fetching; the panel shows a progress bar.

The panel is a non-modal dialog named by label ("Notifications"); focus moves into it on open and back to the bell on close. Escape, a press outside, the close button or the bell close it. Each day is a list. The bell's name includes the unread count ("Notifications, 3 unread"). When unread notifications arrive while the panel is closed, a polite live region announces "2 new notifications".

label: Notification Manager
summary: A toast queue: shows transient messages as a stack of snackbars in the browser's top layer.
overview:
The manager shows each toast as a wc-snackbar in a region in the browser's top layer, fixed to the viewport at placement, above sticky headers and open modals. A toast is removed from the page once its exit animation ends.

Every toast hides itself after its duration (5000 ms by default; the timer pauses while the pointer or focus is on it) unless it has an action or duration: 0, whether it is dismissible or not.

Show a toast with manager.show({ title, intent }), which returns its id, or from anywhere with a peacock-toast window event whose detail holds the same options plus target (the manager's name; unset goes to the manager named global) and callback(id). Hide toasts with manager.hide(id) or a peacock-toast-dismiss window event with detail.notifications, an array of ids.

label: Page Header
summary: The top of a page: title, supporting text, breadcrumb, actions, metadata and tabs.
overview:
Page header names the page with headline, an <h1> by default (heading-level picks another level, for a header inside a section), and supporting-text under it.

Slots fill the rest: breadcrumb above the title, start before it (an avatar or icon), meta under it (tags, a status, timestamps), actions at the end (buttons) and tabs along the bottom edge (a wc-tabs). back-href adds a round back link before the title, named by back-label (Back by default).

The header responds to its own width: on narrow containers the actions wrap onto their own row under the title and the headline steps down a size.

```html
  headline="Quarterly report"
  supporting-text="Revenue, costs and headcount for Q3"
  back-href="/reports"
  back-label="All reports"
>
  <wc-breadcrumb slot="breadcrumb">…</wc-breadcrumb>
  <wc-tag slot="meta">Draft</wc-tag>
  <wc-button slot="actions" variant="outlined">Share</wc-button>
  <wc-button slot="actions">Publish</wc-button>
  <wc-tabs slot="tabs">…</wc-tabs>
```

label: Password Rules
summary: A live checklist of password requirements, shown under a new-password field.
overview:
Password rules lists what a new password needs ("At least 12 characters", "One number") and ticks each requirement off as the person types. Each item shows its state with an icon shape and, for screen readers, the words "met" or "not met"; color is never the only cue. Changes are announced politely once typing pauses, and only for the requirements whose state flipped.

Point for at the id of a wc-password-field in the same document or shadow root: the checklist follows the field's input events and, while a typed password fails a rule, sets the field's custom validity, so the form will not submit. An empty field is left to its own required. Without for, set value yourself.

The common rules are attributes with translated labels: minlength, require-uppercase, require-lowercase, require-number and require-symbol. Add your own with the rules property: { id, label, test }, where test is a RegExp or a function. They are listed after the built-in ones.
fires: change - Dispatched when the password goes from failing to passing or back. `failed` holds the ids of the failing rules.
cssprop: --password-rules-unmet-color - Icon color of an unmet rule.
example:
```html
<wc-password-field id="new-password" label="New password" autocomplete="new-password" required></wc-password-field>
<wc-password-rules for="new-password" minlength="12" require-number require-symbol></wc-password-rules>
```

customElement.description: Whether `value` passes `rule`. Stateless, even for a global pattern.

label: Phone Field
summary: A field for a phone number, with a country selector for the calling code.
overview:
Phone field has a country selector at its start, showing the flag and calling code (such as +44), and a field for the national number. Its value is the whole number in E.164 form (+442079460958), ready to store or dial, or '' while the field holds no valid number. A full international number typed or pasted into the field (starting with + or 00, such as +44 20 7946 0958) selects its country and leaves the national part. A leading trunk 0 (020 7946 0958) is dropped, except in Italy, Vatican City, San Marino, Côte d'Ivoire and Congo, which keep it.

The field checks the shape of the number, not whether it exists: digits only (spaces, dashes and brackets are allowed between them), 4 to 15 digits with the calling code, as E.164 allows. Anything else shows "Enter a valid phone number" and blocks form submission, as does an empty required field. Inside a <form> the E.164 value is submitted under its name.

The country list holds every ITU calling code, named in the field's locale (the nearest lang, else the browser's). country starts as the locale's region (so lang="en-GB" starts on the United Kingdom), else the United States. Countries that share a code, such as the +1 countries, keep the one the person selected. Limit or order the list with countries and pin the likely ones to the top with preferred-countries.

label: Pin Input
summary: A row of single-character cells for a one-time code or PIN.
overview:
Pin input takes a code of length characters (6 by default), one per cell. Its value is the code as one string, and inside a <form> it is submitted under its name. The cells sit in one field box, so variant, size, the states and the start/end slots look as on every other field.

type="numeric" (the default) takes digits and shows the numeric keypad on phones; type="alphanumeric" takes the letters A–Z and digits and uppercases letters, so the value is what the cells show. Anything else is ignored, so a pasted or autofilled 123-456 or G-123456 fills 123456. masked hides the characters like a password.

The first cell has autocomplete="one-time-code", so a code from a text message can be filled in by the phone. Typing moves to the next cell and typing over a filled cell replaces it. Backspace clears the cell, or, in an empty cell, the one before it; Delete clears the cell. Left, Right, Home and End move between cells, and Tab leaves the row. The code is always filled from the start: a cell after the first empty one cannot be focused. The cells always run left to right, as codes are written, also in right-to-left pages.

Validation: with required an empty code is valueMissing; a code that is started but not complete is tooShort (whether required or not), like text under a native minlength. The message shows once the code is committed or the form is submitted.

label: Popover
summary: Displays rich content, such as text with actions, in a floating panel anchored to a trigger element.
overview:
The Popover component wraps a trigger element and a wc-popover-content child. The panel opens in the browser's top layer, so it shows above modals, sheets, menus and any parent with overflow: hidden; floating-ui keeps it next to the trigger and inside the viewport.

The panel is a non-modal dialog: Escape closes it, and so does a press outside the trigger and the panel (no-light-dismiss turns that off). Name it with label or with an element in the content's heading slot. With trigger="click" or "hover" the trigger gets aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-controls and aria-expanded; with "manual" the component that opens the popover owns the trigger's ARIA.

Use a popover, not a wc-tooltip, for rich content with actions.

fires: close - Fired when the popover closes: Escape, a press outside, the trigger (a second click, or the pointer leaving a hover trigger is `light-dismiss`), or `hide()` / `open = false`.
example:

```html Open popover
Popover body text goes here.

 ```

label: Presence Indicator
summary: A small online, away, busy or offline dot on the corner of a person's avatar.
overview:
A presence indicator shows whether a person is available, in chat, collaboration and people lists. Wrap an avatar in it and the dot sits on the avatar's bottom-end corner (bottom right, or bottom left in right-to-left pages) inside a ring of the surface color, sized to the avatar:

<wc-presence-indicator status="online">
  <wc-avatar name="Ana Lima"></wc-avatar>
</wc-presence-indicator>

status is online, away, busy or offline (the default). Each has its own shape as well as its own color, so it does not rest on color alone, and forced-colors mode keeps the shapes: a filled circle (online), a crescent moon (away), a circle with a dash (busy) and a hollow ring (offline).

The status is part of the person's name, not a separate announcement: a wrapped wc-avatar is named "Ana Lima, online" (its label attribute, else its name, then the status). Other wrapped content, such as an img, is followed by the status as screen-reader text. On its own, without content, the dot is an image named by the status. label replaces the status text, such as "In a meeting".

size follows the wrapped avatar's size; set it for a dot on its own, or to override.

Which one to use: wc-presence-indicator for a person's availability, attached to their avatar, where the four statuses and their shapes are fixed and people recognise them from chat apps. wc-status-indicator for the state of a thing (a service, a job, a device) shown as a dot and a visible label next to its name, with the general intents (info, success, warning, danger). A person's status written out in a list or a profile ("Away") can be either; prefer the status indicator when the label is visible.
cssprop: --presence-indicator-ring-color - Color of the ring around the dot and of its holes; defaults to the surface color. Set it to the background behind the avatar.

summary: The box for writing to the assistant: plain text with mentions, sent with Enter, with a Stop button while the answer arrives.
overview:
Where people ask the assistant for something, at the bottom of wc-assistant-panel (ADR-030002). It is plain text, no formatting: Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line, and the box grows up to max-rows lines.

Sending fires a cancelable submit with the text in detail.value and its mentions in detail.mentions, then empties the box unless the event is cancelled. While loading (the answer is arriving), the send button becomes Stop, which fires stop, and Enter does not send.

Mentions point the assistant at records: with triggers="@" (the default), typing @ fires search; answer by setting suggestions, as on wc-mention-input. Add / to triggers for commands. A mention is stored as [@INC-2318](mention:inc_2318).

summary: Groups radios under one label, one name and one value.
overview:
Radio group gives its wc-radio children a shared name (its own, or a generated one), so only one can be checked. Its value is the value of the checked radio, and setting it checks the matching radio.

The radios stay form-associated, so the group submits once, through the checked radio. disabled, readonly and required are passed to every radio; a required group blocks form submission until a radio is checked.

Below the radios the group shows helper-text, or error-text while error is set, or the radios' validation message after a failed check (reportValidity() or a form submission).

label: Rating
summary: A star rating: pick how many stars, or show an average such as 4.3 out of 5.
overview:
Rating lets the person pick a score from 1 to max (5 by default) by clicking a star or with the keyboard. Pointing at the stars previews the score; nothing changes until the click. With precision="0.5" the left half of a star (the right half in right-to-left layouts) picks a half star. With clearable, choosing the current score again clears it.

It is one keyboard stop that follows the WAI-ARIA slider pattern: the arrow keys change the score by one step (mirrored in right-to-left layouts), Home and End go to the lowest and highest score, and the digit keys pick that many stars. Screen readers hear "3 out of 5".

readonly turns it into a display, for example a product's average review: any value is drawn with a partly filled star, and it is a single image named "Rated 4.3 out of 5". Inside a <form> the score is submitted under name; no score submits nothing, and required blocks submission until one is picked.

The stars are Material Symbols: icon names the empty shape and <icon>-fill the filled one, so any symbol with a fill variant works (favorite, thumb_up).

label: Redvars Loader
summary: A loading indicator drawn from the Redvars r mark, for app start-up and full-page loads.
overview:
Redvars Loader animates the r mark on its red tile in one of five ways (variant): build (the default: the stem rises and the arm swings out), trace (the outline draws itself and fills), fill (the r fills from the bottom), pulse (the tile beats and sends out a ring) and orbit (a runner chases round the tile).

With value (0 to 100) it stops looping and fills the r to that level, as a determinate progress bar. It is role="progressbar", named by label ("Loading" by default).

The full animation plays by default: it is the point of the loader. With respect-reduced-motion, a system that asks for reduced motion gets a slow fill of the r instead, with nothing moving.

For loading inside a page, use wc-circular-progress or wc-linear-progress; this one is the brand moment, such as the first load of an app.

label: Relative Time
summary: A date and time shown relative to now, such as "5 minutes ago" or "in 3 days", that keeps itself current.
overview:
wc-relative-time shows datetime (ISO 8601, such as 2026-11-07T08:00:00Z) relative to now with Intl.RelativeTimeFormat in the resolved locale (locale, else the nearest lang, else the browser's): "now", "5 minutes ago", "yesterday", "in 3 days". It renders a <time datetime> whose tooltip (title) is the absolute date and time, such as "Nov 7, 2026, 8:00 AM".

numeric="always" says "1 day ago" instead of "yesterday". format-style is long (the default, "5 minutes ago"), short ("5 min. ago") or narrow ("5m ago"). (It is not style, which is the HTML attribute for inline CSS.)

absolute-after is an ISO 8601 duration such as P7D (7 days) or PT12H: times farther from now than that show as a date instead, such as "Nov 2" (with the year when it is not this year). Without it the time is always relative.

The text stays current: every wc-relative-time on the page shares one timer, which refreshes each one as often as its text can change (every 10 seconds under a minute, every minute under an hour, less often after that) and pauses while the page is hidden.

Content inside the element is the fallback, shown while datetime is missing or not a date, and before the component loads.
cssprop: --relative-time-text-color - Color of the text; defaults to the surrounding text color.
example:
```html
<wc-relative-time datetime="2026-11-07T08:00:00Z">Nov 7, 2026</wc-relative-time>
<wc-relative-time datetime="2026-11-06T08:00:00Z" numeric="always"></wc-relative-time>
<wc-relative-time datetime="2026-11-07T08:00:00Z" format-style="short"></wc-relative-time>
<wc-relative-time datetime="2026-10-02T08:00:00Z" absolute-after="P7D"></wc-relative-time>
```

label: Resizable Panels
summary: A split view whose panes the person resizes by dragging the dividers between them.
overview:
Resizable panels lays out its wc-panel children in a row (orientation="horizontal", the default) or a column ("vertical"), with a divider between each pair: a list beside its detail, an editor above its preview. Each panel's size is its share in percent, bounded by min-size and max-size. Dragging a divider resizes the two panels beside it; in right-to-left layouts horizontal drags mirror.

A collapsible panel collapses to its collapsed-size when dragged well past its minimum, and a double-click or Enter on the divider collapses or restores it.

Each divider is a focusable role="separator" whose value is the size of the panel before it. The arrow keys along the split move it by 1% (10% with Shift), Home and End move it to the panel's minimum and maximum, and Enter collapses or restores.

input fires while a divider moves and change when the drag ends or a key moves it, with every panel's size. Set autosave to a key to keep the layout in local storage and restore it on the next visit. A panel can hold another split view.

label: Scroll Area
summary: A scroll container with thin themed scrollbars and shadows at the edges that have more content.
overview:
wc-scroll-area scrolls its content natively (the browser does the scrolling, so touch, wheel, keyboard and scroll snapping behave as usual) with thin scrollbars in the theme's colors, and a soft shadow at each edge that has more content beyond it, so people can see there is more. The shadows follow the scroll position with a scroll-driven animation where the browser supports one, and a scroll listener elsewhere.

Give the scroll area a size, such as block-size or max-block-size for a vertical one: it scrolls what does not fit. orientation is vertical (the default), horizontal or both.

When the content overflows, the scroll area is focusable (tabindex="0"), so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down. Give it a label that says what it holds, such as "Terms of service": it is then a region landmark with that name, which screen readers announce on focus.

label: Select
summary: A field that opens a list of options to pick one or several from, with optional search as you type.
overview:
Select builds on wc-field and wc-menu to provide a fully-featured dropdown picker.

  • Single and multi-select modes; a multi-select shows a checkbox on every option.
  • Client-side typeahead with search="contains".
  • Server-side typeahead with search="managed": listen to search, replace the options and set loading while they load; "No results" shows when the search leaves no option.
  • allow-custom keeps typed text that matches no option as the value, through a "Create …" row (or Enter in the search input) that fires create.
  • Multi-select chips on one row, with a "+N" chip for the ones that do not fit.
  • clearable adds a button that clears the value.
  • Form-associated: submits the value under name (one entry per value with multiple).
  • Validates like a native select: required with nothing selected blocks form submission, and the message shows under the field once a value is committed or the form is submitted.
  • The options open in the top layer, so a select works inside a wc-modal.

Options come from <wc-option> children or from the options property; use one or the other. When both are given, both are shown: the options built from options follow the children, and for a value present in both, the child (first in order) gives the label.

Keyboard: Enter, Space, Arrow Down or Arrow Up open the options and focus the selected one. While closed, typing a letter selects the next option starting with it and Home or End select the first or last option (single select, like a native select). In the list, the arrows move, typing a letter jumps to the next option starting with it, Enter or Space picks, Escape closes and returns focus to the field. With search, typing goes to the search input; Arrow Down moves into the list and Enter picks the first match (with allow-custom, the typed text unless an option's label matches it exactly).
slot: end - Trailing content, before the dropdown arrow.
fires: create - Dispatched when the person keeps typed text that matches no option (`allow-custom`). Cancel it to keep the value unchanged, for example to add the option yourself.
example:
```html
<wc-select label="Fruit" placeholder="Pick a fruit...">
  <wc-option value="apple">Apple</wc-option>
  <wc-option value="banana">Banana</wc-option>
</wc-select>
```

label: Side Sheet
summary: A panel that slides in from the start or end edge of the screen with extra content, either modal over the page or beside it.
overview:
The sheet renders a native <dialog>. The modal variant (the default) opens it with showModal(): it renders in the browser's top layer above the page, with a scrim; the rest of the page is inert and does not scroll; focus moves to the first element with autofocus inside it and returns where it was when the sheet closes. Escape and a click on the scrim close it (no-light-dismiss keeps it open on scrim clicks).

The standard variant opens the dialog with show(): it is not modal, stays in the page flow beside the content (place it in a flex row), and does not trap focus, lock scrolling or close on Escape.

placement is logical: end is the right edge in left-to-right pages and the left edge in right-to-left pages.

fires: close - Fired when the sheet closes: Escape, a scrim click, the close button, or `hide()`.
example:
```html
<wc-button onclick="document.getElementById('filters').show()">Filters</wc-button>
<wc-side-sheet id="filters" heading="Filters">
  <wc-checkbox autofocus>In stock only</wc-checkbox>
  <wc-checkbox>Free shipping</wc-checkbox>
  <wc-button onclick="this.closest('wc-side-sheet').hide()">Apply</wc-button>
</wc-side-sheet>
```

label: Signature Pad
summary: An area to sign with a mouse, finger or pen, or by typing a name.
overview:
Signature pad records a handwritten signature. Strokes are smoothed, and a pen draws thicker the harder it presses. The undo button removes the last stroke and the clear button starts over. Strokes are stored as points, so the pad can resize with its container, and draws at the screen's pixel density, without blurring.

A signature cannot be drawn with a keyboard, so the pad also takes a typed name: the "Type your name instead" button shows a name field, and the name is drawn on the pad in a script font (--signature-pad-font-family). The drawing is announced as "Signature, empty" or "Signature, signed".

value is the signature as a PNG data URL with a transparent background, or '' while the pad is empty; change fires after each stroke. Inside a <form> it is submitted under name as a PNG file, like a file input, so the server receives an upload rather than a long base64 string. required blocks submission until the person signs. toDataURL(), toBlob() and fromDataURL() export and load images.

On screen the ink follows the theme (--signature-pad-ink-color, light in dark mode). Exports always use --signature-pad-export-ink-color, black by default, so a signature made in dark mode does not come out white on a white document.
fires: change - Dispatched after each stroke, undo and clear, and when a typed name is committed.

overview:
Site footer is the page's contentinfo landmark. The brand slot and the wc-site-footer-group columns sit at the top; a bottom row holds the legal slot (copyright and policy links) and the social slot (icon buttons that link to the site's profiles).

Slots that are empty take no room, so the same component is a full website footer or a slim portal footer with one row of text and links.

The footer responds to its own width, not the viewport's: narrower than 48rem the columns wrap two to a row, and narrower than 24rem they stack. Links stay visible at every width, one tap away, rather than folded into an accordion.

summary: The top navigation bar of a website or portal: brand, links, menus and actions.
overview:
Site header is the banner of a site: the brand at the start, the site's navigation, and actions such as Sign in or a call to action at the end. It is for websites and portals. For an application's own chrome use wc-app-bar, and for a bar at the bottom of a phone screen wc-navigation-bar.

Put wc-site-nav-link elements in it for destinations and wc-site-nav-menu elements for sections with several pages. A menu is a disclosure button that opens a panel of links, as a list or, with layout="columns", as columns of wc-site-nav-group with a featured card. These are links and disclosure buttons, not an ARIA menu, so Tab moves through them as through any links.

When the header is narrower than collapse-at (720px by default), or too narrow for the bar's content to fit, the links and menus move into a drawer that slides in from the start edge, opened by a menu button. The actions slot moves to the bottom of the drawer; the end slot stays in the bar, for something that must always show, such as a user menu or one short button.

A visually hidden Skip to main content link is the first focusable element. It moves focus to skip-target (#main by default).

label: Site Nav Menu
summary: A section of a site header that opens a panel of links.
overview:
A disclosure button in a wc-site-header that shows a panel of wc-site-nav-link elements under the bar. The default layout="list" is a short list under the button. layout="columns" is a wide panel of wc-site-nav-group columns, with an optional featured card in the feature slot.

It follows the disclosure navigation pattern, not the ARIA menu pattern: the button has aria-expanded, and the links follow it in the Tab order while the panel is open. Click, Enter or Space opens the panel; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button, and so does a click outside or moving focus out of it. Only one menu in a header is open at a time. Arrow Down on the button opens the panel at its first link, and the arrow keys, Home and End move between the links.

The menu shows as current when one of its links is current. When the header is collapsed into its drawer, the menu becomes an expandable section of the drawer, expanded when it holds the current page.

fires: close - Dispatched when the person closes the panel: the button, Escape, or a click or focus outside.
cssprop: --site-nav-menu-columns-max-width - Widest a `columns` panel grows. Defaults to 60rem.
example:
```html

  <wc-site-nav-group label="Build">
    <wc-site-nav-link href="/tables" description="Describe data, get secured screens">
```

label: Skeleton
summary: A placeholder shape that stands in for content that has not arrived yet.
overview:
A skeleton fills the size you give it and, while visible is set, shows a sweeping animation. Size it to match the content it replaces, and match its corners with the --skeleton-container-shape properties, for example round for an avatar. It ignores pointer events.

A skeleton is a look, not a busy state: a component working on something uses loading. Chips, list items and buttons have their own skeleton attribute for this placeholder look.

this placeholder look.

label: Slider
summary: A track with a thumb the person drags to pick a number from a range.
overview:
The slider is form-associated: its value is submitted under its name, and form.reset() restores the starting value. Without a value it starts at the middle of min–max, like a native range input.

label is shown above the track, as on fields, and names the thumb; without it the thumb is named "Slider". value-text (the valueText property) formats the value for aria-valuetext and the visible value, for example v => `${v}%`.

required does not apply: a slider always has a value. readonly keeps it focusable but its value cannot change.

Keyboard: the arrows move one step (ten with Shift), Page Up and Page Down move ten steps, Home and End go to min and max.

label: Snackbar
summary: A brief message at the bottom of the screen about something the app did, with an optional action, that hides itself.
overview:
An open snackbar is shown as a manual popover, so it renders in the browser's top layer, above sticky headers, app bars and open modals whatever their z-index. Opening it again while it is visible brings it back in front of anything opened since. Opening one snackbar closes any other open snackbar; use wc-notification-manager to show several at once.

It hides itself after duration milliseconds. The timer pauses while the pointer is over the snackbar or focus is inside it, and starts again when both leave. A snackbar with an action (action-label) or duration="0" does not hide by itself, so there is time to reach the action.

It is a polite live region (role="status"); intent="danger" makes it assertive (role="alert"). With dismissible, a close button is shown and Escape closes it while focus is inside it.


label: Sparkline
summary: A tiny inline chart without axes that shows the shape of a series, for example in a KPI tile or a table cell.
overview:
Sparkline draws data (an array of numbers) as a line, an area or bars. It has no axes, labels or tooltips: it shows a trend at a glance, next to the number it explains. Values that are not finite numbers are skipped.

It fills its own box, which defaults to 6rem by 1.5rem; set width and height in CSS to change it. The line keeps its stroke width however the box is stretched. highlight-last marks the latest value with a dot (or, for bars, dims the others). A flat series is drawn across the middle, and an empty one draws nothing.

A screen reader reads it as one image: the label and then a summary, for example "Signups, Trend from 12 to 18, high 21, low 9". format formats those numbers, in the nearest lang.

label: Stack
summary: Lays out its children in a column or a row, with a gap on the spacing scale.
overview:
The stack is a flex container: the element itself has display: flex, so its children are the flex items, with no wrapper between them. direction is vertical (a column, the default) or horizontal (a row, which follows the writing direction, so it runs right to left in RTL).

gap takes a step of the spacing token scale: gap="200" is var(--spacing-200). The steps are 000, 025, 050, 075, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400, 500, 600, 800, 1000, 1200 and 2000. Without gap there is none. A style="gap: …" on the element still wins.

align sets align-items and justify sets justify-content; wrap lets the items wrap onto more lines.

collapse-below makes a horizontal stack lay out vertically while the stack itself is narrower than the given width (pixels, or a length in px, rem or em). It measures the stack, not the viewport, so it works in sidebars and cards; the collapsed property and the :state(collapsed) selector tell when it applies.
slot: - The items to lay out.
example:
```html
<wc-stack direction="horizontal" gap="200" align="center" collapse-below="30rem">
  <wc-avatar name="Ada Lovelace"></wc-avatar>
  <wc-text>Ada Lovelace</wc-text>
  <wc-button>Follow</wc-button>
</wc-stack>
```
