label: Stat
summary: A KPI tile: a labelled number with its change since the last period.
overview:
Stat shows one metric: a label ("Monthly revenue") and a value, formatted with Intl.NumberFormat in the nearest lang using format (for example {"style": "currency", "currency": "USD"}).

The tile fills the width it is given, like a card, and its value gets smaller in a narrow tile rather than wrapping. Place stats in a wc-grid or give them a width; in a flex row, give each flex: 1.

The change comes from previous, the value of the last period, or is given as delta. delta-format="percent" (the default) shows it as a share of the previous value; with delta it is then a fraction, so 0.08 is 8%. delta-format="absolute" shows the amount, formatted like the value. An arrow shows the direction, and the color whether it is good: green when the value moves the positive way (up by default), red when it moves the other way. Set positive="down" for metrics such as churn, or none for neutral ones. comparison names the period ("vs last month").

A screen reader reads the tile as one sentence, for example "Monthly revenue, $12,400, up 8% from last period". help adds an info button with a tooltip, loading shows a placeholder, and the trend slot holds a wc-sparkline. variant="plain" drops the tile's own outline and padding, for a stat inside a wc-card.

cssprop: --stat-container-shape - Corner radius of the tile.
example:
```html

  format='{"style": "percent", "maximumFractionDigits": 1}'></wc-stat>
```

label: Status Indicator
summary: A small dot and label for the state of a system or an entity, such as "Operational" or "Offline".
overview:
A status indicator shows the state of something: a service, a device, a sync job, a person's presence. intent (info, success, warning, danger; unset is neutral) picks the color and the shape of the dot (a square, circle, triangle, diamond, or a ring for neutral), so it does not rest on color alone, and forced-colors mode keeps the shapes. label is the text next to the dot, such as "Degraded"; always give one, it is what the indicator says.

pulse animates the dot for a live or in-progress state ("Syncing", "Recording"); the animation is off when the person asks for reduced motion. dot-only hides the label where there is no room, such as a dense table column: the label is then still read by screen readers and shown as a tooltip.

By default the indicator is plain text, read where it stands. Set live when its status changes while the person is on the page and the change should be announced: it gets role="status", a polite live region. Do not set it on many indicators at once, such as every row of a table, or the announcements pile up.

Which one to use: wc-status-indicator for the state of a thing, read next to its name ("API: Operational"). wc-badge for a count or an unread dot attached to another element, such as an icon button. wc-tag for a label or a category in a filled container ("Draft", "Design"), often several side by side.

Step is one entry in a wc-stepper. A screen reader reads each step as its position, label and state, for example "Step 2 of 4, Shipping, Completed".

label: Stepper
summary: Shows progress through a multi-step flow, such as a wizard, onboarding or checkout.
overview:
Stepper shows where the person is in a flow; the app renders each step's content itself. current names the current step by its value (a step without one is named by its zero-based index, so current="1" is the second step). An empty or unknown current means the first step. Steps before the current one are complete and later ones upcoming; each step can add error, disabled or optional.

By default (navigation="none") the stepper is a plain list and the app moves it with current, next() and previous(). With navigation="free" every step that is not disabled is a button; with navigation="linear" only the steps up to the first unfinished required step are, so the person can go back but not skip ahead. Activating a step fires a cancelable change and then moves current. The steps are one tab stop: the arrow keys (mirrored in right-to-left layouts), Home and End move between them, and Enter or Space activates one.

```html
  <wc-step label="Billing" error error-text="Card declined"></wc-step>

```

label: Sub Menu
summary: Connects a menu item to a nested menu.
overview:
Put it inside a wc-menu, with a wc-menu-item in the item slot and a wc-menu in the menu slot. The nested menu opens beside the item (on the left in right-to-left pages), takes the parent menu's variant, and the item gets aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls.

Clicking the item opens or closes the nested menu. Resting the pointer on it opens the menu after hover-open-delay (120ms) without moving focus, and leaving closes it after hover-close-delay (180ms).

ArrowRight (ArrowLeft in right-to-left pages), Enter or Space on the item opens the nested menu and focuses its first enabled item. Escape or ArrowLeft (ArrowRight in right-to-left pages) closes it and returns focus to the item. Choosing an item in the nested menu closes the parent menu too. show() and close() open and close it from code.

Renders an inline SVG fetched from a URL, with lazy loading via IntersectionObserver and an optional click-to-preview lightbox.

  • alt is the text alternative, as on a native <img>: with it the SVG is role="img"; without it, it is decorative.
  • preview opens the SVG enlarged in a modal lightbox on click. Focus moves to its close button, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the SVG.
  • --svg-color, or the inherited color, tints the SVG; --svg-size sets its size.

label: Tab
summary: One tab in a row of tabs, with an optional icon and badge; with a link address it navigates instead.
overview:
A tab in a wc-tabs list renders a control with role="tab" and aria-selected; inside a wc-tab-group the control also points at its panel.

A tab with href is a link, not a tab: it renders a plain <a> with aria-current="page" when selected. Tabs that navigate between pages are navigation, so put link tabs in a <nav>.

label: Tab Group
summary: Pairs a row of tabs with their panels and shows the panel of the selected tab.
overview:
Tabs and panels are matched by value (<wc-tab value="billing"> shows <wc-tab-panel value="billing">), or by position when no tab has a value.

The group wires the tabs pattern: each panel is labelled by its tab, and each tab points at its panel. Tabs and panels added later are wired too. When the wc-tabs is managed, the group leaves the selection to the consumer.

label: Table
summary: A data table with sorting, row selection, resizable and reorderable columns, inline editing and paging.
overview:
The table displays rows of data with sorting (also by several columns), row selection, a sticky header, sticky start or end columns, and columns the user can resize, reorder and hide.

It follows the grid keyboard pattern: the table is one tab stop and the arrow keys move between cells. Space selects the focused row, Enter activates the focused cell, and Ctrl+C copies its text. On a column header, Shift+Enter adds a sort level and Alt+Left/Right moves a reorderable column.

Put a wc-pagination in the footer slot to page the rows. When rows are selected, a bar over the header shows the count and the actions placed in the bulk-actions slot.

Rows can expand into a detail row (detailTemplate), be grouped under collapsible headers (group-by), and be edited in place (editable columns). Columns can show a footer aggregate (aggregate). virtual renders only the rows in view, for large data sets, and exportCsv() returns the rows as CSV.

Dispatched when a cell is clicked or activated with Enter. Detail: `{ record, column, altKey, ctrlKey, metaKey, shiftKey }`.

label: Tab Panel
summary: The content of one tab, shown while that tab is selected.
overview: The panel has role="tabpanel"; inside a wc-tab-group it is labelled by its tab (aria-labelledby) and shown while that tab is selected. It is focusable, so keyboard users reach the content right after the tab list.

label: Tabs
summary: The row of tabs, which the person moves between by clicking or with the arrow keys.
overview:
Tabs holds the tab buttons and manages their layout. It follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: the host has role="tablist" (give it an aria-label), only the selected tab is a tab stop, and the Left and Right arrow keys (mirrored in right-to-left layouts), Home and End move between tabs. Moving to a tab selects it, so its panel shows at once. Disabled tabs are skipped.

With managed, the tabs do not change the selection themselves: they fire change and the consumer sets selected on the chosen tab.

When every tab is a link (href), the tabs are navigation rather than a tablist: the host gets no tablist role, so wrap it in a <nav>.

label: Tag
summary: A read-only label for a status or a value.
overview: A tag shows a status or a value; it has no action of its own. Use intent (info, success, warning, danger) when the tag means something, and accent for a decorative hue (categories, labels). For a removable or selectable item use wc-chip.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Tag size. Possible values are `"sm"`, `"md"`, `"lg"`. Defaults to `"md"`.

label: Textarea
summary: A multi-line text field that can grow with its content.
overview:
Textarea is form-associated: inside a <form> its value is submitted under its name, and form.reset() restores the starting value.

It validates like a native textarea: required, minlength and maxlength block form submission, and the message shows under the field once the value is committed or the form is submitted. With maxlength a character counter shows under the field.

rows sets the starting height. With auto-grow the height follows the content, up to max-rows when it is set; resize controls whether the person can drag the corner to resize it.

With ai-completion and a provider that offers completions (ADR-030002), a pause in typing at the end of a line shows ghost text: how the assistant would go on, in grey after the caret. Tab takes it, Ctrl+→ (⌘→) takes a word, Escape or typing dismisses it. Nothing is inserted until the person takes it, and sensitive fields never ask.

It is a building block, not a form control: it has no name and is not submitted with a form. In a form, use wc-time-field or wc-datetime-field.

label: Toolbar
summary: A group of related actions, such as editor formatting controls.
overview:
The toolbar groups related actions into one control. The floating variant (default) is an elevated pill that sits over content, such as a canvas or a selection. The flat variant has no container of its own, for embedding in existing chrome like a card or editor header. Both variants lay their actions out horizontally or vertically.

Render actions directly as children. Use a wc-divider to separate groups of actions; in a horizontal toolbar give it orientation="vertical".

The toolbar follows the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern: it is a single tab stop, and the arrow keys along its orientation move focus between actions (Home and End jump to the first and last). Disabled actions and dividers are skipped. Give the toolbar an aria-label.
cssprop: --toolbar-wrap - `wrap` lets actions flow onto more lines when the toolbar is narrow. Defaults to `nowrap`.
example:
```html
<!-- Flat toolbar inside existing chrome -->
<wc-toolbar variant="flat" aria-label="Row actions">
  <wc-icon-button variant="text" color="surface" aria-label="Edit"><wc-icon name="edit"></wc-icon></wc-icon-button>
  <wc-icon-button variant="text" color="surface" aria-label="Delete"><wc-icon name="delete"></wc-icon></wc-icon-button>
</wc-toolbar>
```

label: Tooltip
summary: A short text label shown next to an element on hover or keyboard focus.
overview:
A short text label shown next to its target on hover or focus. It opens in the browser's top layer, so it shows above modals and menus, and describes the target through aria-describedby. Escape hides a visible tooltip without closing the dialog or menu around it.

The target is the element whose id is in for, looked up in the tooltip's own document or shadow root, or else the parent element. When the target is in another shadow root, the link uses ariaDescribedByElements where the browser supports it; elsewhere the target is not described.

Use wc-popover for rich content with actions.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description:
The ID of the element the tooltip should attach to.
If not provided, it defaults to the parent element.

attributes.name: trigger
attributes.description: What shows the tooltip: any of `hover`, `focus` and `click`, separated by spaces.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the tooltip is visible.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description:
Preferred placement relative to the target: `top`, `bottom`, `start` or `end`, optionally with
`-start` or `-end` alignment. `start` and `end` follow the writing direction.

label: Tour
summary: A product tour: a sequence of popups that point at parts of the page, with a spotlight on each.
overview:
Give the tour its steps as data: each has a target (an element id or a CSS selector), a headline, a body and an optional placement. start() shows the first step: the target scrolls into view (instantly when the person prefers reduced motion), a spotlight cut out of a dimmed scrim marks it, and a popup next to it shows "Step 2 of 5", the text, Back, Next (Done on the last step) and a close button that skips the tour. floating-ui flips and shifts the popup so it stays in view. A step without target is centered on the page.

A step whose target is not on the page is skipped in the direction of travel, with a console warning once per target, so a tour survives a missing feature or a collapsed panel.

The popup is a non-modal dialog (role="dialog", named by the headline, described by the body). The scrim is only drawn, never hit: clicks reach the page, so the person can try the highlighted control while the tour explains it, which a modal tour would block by making the page inert. Focus moves into the popup at each step and back to where it was when the tour ends. Escape ends the tour; Left and Right (mirrored in right-to-left layouts) go back and forward while focus is in the popup.

Methods: start(index = 0), next(), previous(), end(). step-change fires with detail.index each time a step shows, and close with detail.reason ('escape', 'action' for Done or the close button, 'api') and detail.completed, true when the person finished the last step. Store that to avoid showing a finished tour again.

label: Transfer List
summary: Two lists side by side; the person moves items from "Available" to "Selected" to choose them.
overview:
A transfer list chooses several items from a long list, such as roles for a user, columns for a report or members of a group, where seeing what is chosen next to what is left matters. The items come from options; the ones in the "Selected" list are the value. For a short list use wc-listbox multiple or wc-checkbox-group; inside a compact form use wc-select multiple.

Each list is a wc-listbox multiple, so its keyboard and ARIA work as there: Up and Down move, Space (or a click) checks an item, Ctrl+A (Cmd+A) checks all. The buttons between the lists move the checked items, or all items, to the other list. Enter or a double click moves one item straight away. Disabled options stay where they are, so a disabled selected option is locked in. searchable adds a search box above each list; the buttons then act on the matching items only. Each move is announced, such as "2 items moved to Selected".

Without ordered the value keeps the order of options. With ordered the selected list keeps the person's order: moved items join at the end, the Move up and Move down buttons move the checked items, and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused one.

The value follows wc-listbox multiple: value is a comma-separated list (so option values must not contain commas) and values the same as an array. Inside a <form> each value is submitted under name; required blocks submission while nothing is selected, and form.reset() restores the first value. readonly shows the lists without letting the person move items. On a narrow container the lists stack, with the arrows turned to point down and up.

label: Tree
summary: A hierarchy the person expands, navigates and chooses from, such as files or categories.
overview:
The tree follows the WAI-ARIA tree view pattern: the host has role="tree" (with aria-multiselectable for selection="multiple"), each wc-tree-item has role="treeitem" with aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset and, when it has children, aria-expanded. Nest items to give them children.

It is one tab stop. Up and Down move between visible items, Right expands an item or moves to its first child, Left collapses it or moves to its parent (both mirrored in right-to-left), Home and End jump to the first and last item, * expands every sibling, and typing a letter moves to the next item whose label starts with it. Enter or a double-click fires activate, which toggles an item with children unless canceled. Disabled items are skipped.

selection is none (navigate and activate only), single (the selection follows focus, value is the chosen item) or multiple (each item has a checkbox that Space or a click toggles; value is a comma-separated list, also readable as values). Checking an item checks its descendants, and an item is checked when all its children are and indeterminate when only some are. Disabled items keep their state.

For lazy loading, give an item has-children and add its child items when it fires expand; it shows loading until they arrive.
slot: - `wc-tree-item` elements.
fires: activate - Dispatched from an item on Enter or double-click. Cancel it to keep an item with children from toggling.

example:
```html
<wc-tree label="Permissions" selection="multiple" value="users.read">
  <wc-tree-item value="users" label="Users" expanded>
    <wc-tree-item value="users.read" label="Read"></wc-tree-item>
    <wc-tree-item value="users.write" label="Write"></wc-tree-item>
  </wc-tree-item>
</wc-tree>
```

label: Tree chart
summary: A hierarchy laid out as a tidy tree on an infinite canvas: org charts, taxonomies, sitemaps, decision trees.
overview:
Set items to a flat list where each item names its parentId; the chart lays the tree out with each card's real size. Top to bottom by default, or left to right with orientation="horizontal". compact stacks teams with no further levels in a column under their manager, which keeps wide organisations narrow.

A card shows an avatar (or an icon), a headline, supporting text and a badge. Put your own card in slot="item:<id>". The chip under a card shows how many items are below it and expands or collapses them (expand and collapse fire). For lazy loading, give an item hasChildren and add its children when it fires expand; it shows a spinner until they arrive.

search(text) expands the way to every match, highlights the path from the root and dims the rest, and zooms to the first match; clearSearch() undoes it.

With editable, drag a card onto another to change its parent (never into its own branch), add an item below or beside with the buttons on a card, and delete with Delete, which moves the item's children up to its parent. reparent, add and delete fire first and can be canceled; every edit then fires change with the new items. Undo with Ctrl+Z. Expanding, collapsing and edits glide.

The tree follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern with one tab stop. In a vertical chart Up goes to the parent, Down to the first child, Left and Right to siblings (mirrored in right-to-left); a horizontal chart turns the keys. Home and End go to the first and last item, * expands all siblings, Enter selects and Shift + Enter expands or collapses. The canvas is infinite like wc-diagram, with the controls and minimap slots.

label: Typing Indicator

YouTube plays through youtube-nocookie.com and Vimeo with Do Not Track, and a line on the poster says where the video plays from.

Any other src is a video file, shown in the browser's own player with its controls. Put <track> elements in the video for captions and subtitles.

The video keeps its aspect-ratio before and after it loads, so nothing on the page moves.

label: Virtual List
summary: A long list that renders only the items in view, for thousands of items or infinite scroll.
overview:
wc-virtual-list takes an array of items and a renderItem function, and renders only the items in view plus overscan items on each side. Every item has the same height, item-height pixels. The list is its own scroll container: give it a height (the default is 20rem). Scrolling stays inside it at either end, so the page does not start moving under the pointer.

Items are rendered into the list's light DOM, each in a wrapper <div role="listitem">, so page styles reach them. The list manages its children: do not add your own. renderItem returns a Lit template, a DOM node or a string; use arrow functions for event listeners in the template.

The host has role="list" and each rendered item aria-setsize and aria-posinset, so screen readers announce the real length. A focused item stays rendered when it scrolls out of view. With navigable, the items are one tab stop and Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End move focus through the whole list.

For infinite scroll, listen for end-reached, which fires once per length when the last visible item is within threshold items of the end, and append items. The scroll position is kept. Set loading while they load.

label: Workflow
summary: A structured builder for business rules and processes: steps, branches that merge back, parallel paths, loops, error paths and ends.
overview:
Set value to a trigger and a list of steps. Steps are action, wait and end cards, branch and parallel blocks whose paths sit side by side and merge back below (a path that ends draws no merge), and loop frames. An action's onError steps run as a side path. The layout is automatic: top to bottom, or left to right with direction="horizontal", joined by rounded connectors.

Cards show a tinted icon, a headline and the kind of step, up to three fields ({{Step.output}} in a value renders as a data pill), and a footer with outputs, tools or an assignee. density shows less (compact) or everything (expanded). Put your own card in slot="step:<id>".

With editable, a "+" on every connector opens a searchable palette built from stepTypes; step-add fires first and can be canceled to show your own dialog. Drag a step to another "+" to move it, delete it with Delete, duplicate with Ctrl+D, copy and paste, and undo with Ctrl+Z. Steps glide to their new places. Every edit fires change with the new value; selecting a step fires select, for your inspector. Apply its edits with updateStep().

The canvas is infinite, like wc-diagram: pan, zoom, start-position, home(), and the controls and minimap slots. Steps are a tree for screen readers. Up and Down move through steps in reading order, Left and Right move between the paths of a branch (in a horizontal workflow the keys swap), Insert opens the palette after the focused step, Alt + Up or Down moves it, and Shift + Enter collapses or expands a block.

mode="debug" and mode="history" show a run from your engine: each card gets its status and duration, the path taken is drawn solid and paths not taken are dashed, the running step pulses and a dot travels into each step the run reaches (follow keeps it in view). A failed step shows its error with "Retry from here". In debug mode a debug bar fires debug-action (Continue F5, Step over F10, Step into F11, Restart, Stop Shift+F5), and the dot left of each card toggles a breakpoint (F9) and fires breakpoint-toggle. A loop shows an iteration picker; the steps inside show the picked iteration. History mode is read-only. Editing is off outside design. Pair it with wc-workflow-timeline for a timeline of the run.
slot: step:<id> - Custom content for the step with that id, in place of the built-in card.
fires: iteration-change - A different loop iteration was picked. Detail contains `{ loopId, index }`.

label: Workflow timeline
summary: The steps of a workflow run as bars on a shared time scale, in step with a `wc-workflow`.
overview:
Set for to the id of a wc-workflow in debug or history mode: the timeline shows its run, follows its selection, and selects a step in the workflow when a row is clicked. Without a workflow, set value and run yourself.

Each step that ran is a row with its name, a bar from when it started to when it finished (running steps grow to now), coloured by status, and its duration. Steps without a startedAt are laid end to end in reading order.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: Id of the `wc-workflow` to show.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The accessible name and heading. Defaults to "Run timeline".

label: Workspace Switcher
summary: The tenant, organization or project picker at the top of an app's navigation.
overview:
The workspace switcher shows the current workspace (logo or initials, name and a chevron) and opens a menu of the person's workspaces, with a check on the current one. Set workspaces to an array of {value, label, description, avatar} and value to the current workspace's value. Picking another fires change with detail.value; the switcher updates value itself.

The menu starts with a search field that filters the list by name and description (Arrow Down moves into the list, Enter picks the first match); hide-search removes it for short lists. creatable adds a "Create workspace" action at the end, which fires create with the search text, if any, as detail.value.

In a collapsed wc-navigation-rail, set collapsed: the trigger shows only the logo, with the name in a tooltip; open the menu to the side with placement="end-start". The strings, including "workspace", can be renamed per instance through strings, for example for projects.
